passages.provision_quote: A school corporation or charter school may not make available materials that contain: (1) obscene matter (as described in IC 35-49-2-1); or (2) matter harmful to minors (as described in IC 35-49-2-2); within the school library.
passages.note: Enrolled bill text adds a library catalog/removal-request/appeal chapter and bars obscene or harmful-to-minors material in school libraries, but HB 1447 is a multi-subject 'Education matters' act that also covers Muncie schools' exemptions, student surveys, and political-neutrality rules.

Senate roll call 520 shows Donato voting Yea on the Conference Committee Report for HB 1447, a multi-subject education bill, with no statement tying her vote to the library-removal provision specifically.
Bill details page lists Donato as a Senate sponsor of HB 1447, whose official digest describes only the third-party-survey provisions, underscoring the bill's multi-subject nature.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Stacey Donato, Sen. Jeff Raatz

rows.reasoning: HB 1447 (2023) is a multi-subject 'Education matters' act bundling a school-library book-challenge/removal process with unrelated provisions (Muncie schools' exemptions, student surveys, political-neutrality rules, obscenity-law amendments); Donato sponsored it in the Senate and voted Yea on the Conference Committee Report, but no source ties her sponsorship or vote to the library-removal clause specifically, so per the vote ladder (V4.1) the vote/sponsorship proves nothing about that clause on its own and no rung is established.
